newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The relentless speculative attack on South Africa's rand continued apace on Monday, carving another five cents out of its value against the dollar and bringing its loss to 100 cents since February 15 this year.
At the 1400 finish, the rand was pegged a lowest ever 4.6570/6620 against the U.S. dollar from 4.6110/6160 on Friday.
Against the British pound, it sank to a new low 7.5173/5300 from 7.3862 bid late on Friday as cable held its earlier gains to trade above $1.61.
Bewildered dealers again pointed fingers at offshore speculators as the reason behind the rand's slide finding no fundamental reasons for its renewed descent.

The currency began the day fending off dollar demand in a short market. Dealers said London-based demand for the greenback coupled with local importer interest pushed the rand to its morning high of 4.6420 bid against the dollar.

"Once we got above 4.64 some of the banks were liquidating...taking profits," a trader said. Others added that the central Reserve Bank also appeared to have supplied dollars to the market, as had exporters.
The currency maintained a steady course until 1300 GMT, when dealers said renewed offshore dollar interest hammered it again.
After the official close, it probed higher, briefly touching 4.67 bid.
The forward rate in the 12-month area also rose to a record high of 4,975 points, implying a rand/dollar exchange rate of nearly 5.15 against the dollar this time next year.
Charles Jonker at Absa Treasury said the forward market had been discounting at least two one percentage point cuts in interest rates next year.

He said that with the release of higher than expected inflation data last week, poor money and credit numbers, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' comments on Friday that economists were too bullish and president Nelson Mandela's reported threat to resign, the short-term outlook for interest rates was gloomy.
"Overall sentiment with regard to interest rate movements especially has deteriorated a lot," he said.
He expected hard-pressed importers to use any dip in the currency as an opportunity to cover.
"In the very short-term it does not look good," he said.
The bond market also ended weaker in sympathy with the rand, while technical indicators pointed to a move above the key 16 percent level soon.
The key R150 was last pegged at a 15.885 percent yield from 15.73 percent on Friday.
"We have an inverse head and shoulders from a break at 15.45 percent which means we are going to 16.05 percent," a trader said in reference to technical indicators.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners bought a net 757.690 rand worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 48.79 million rand worth on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 6.03 billion rand from 38.24 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 16.15 percent bid and 16 percent offered. The 90-day BA rate was unchanged at between 15.55 and 15.40 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 7.386 billion rand on Saturday from 7.370 billion rand on Friday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
